name: 035.4 — cost, docs, the theme, close
author: brodgar
description: Self-checking suite for task 035.4, the close of feature C2: a THEME IS DATA — chrome included — and painting it costs NO Lua. Reads a theme.json shaped exactly like the bundled `theme` example's file and asserts what a file can and cannot carry: the chrome arrives as plain data (a 1-indexed colour array, a 9-slice's four insets, a pad in pixels) while an image is a path, because an image is a HANDLE and so is a font's face — the only two values JSON cannot hold, and the whole adapter a JSON theme needs is the three lines that map them. Mapped, the file is one sheet carrying site keys, chrome and a tree key together; it applies, and the proof that nothing between the file and the client interprets anything is ARITHMETIC: a probe window measures content + the file's own insets + twice the file's own pad, to the pixel, with its content starting one pad inside those insets, and the file's tree key resolves on the one window it names (readable back through widget:style(), which is how any cascade level that names a window reaches that window's chrome). Dropping the sheet restores the exact numbers it found, leaves the probe resolving nil again and leaves no sheet-fed chrome anywhere in the client. The cost half is the feature's other standing claim, measured through hafen.client:profiling() over the SAME windows twice — the round stands up four of its own rather than measure whatever happens to be open, so the difference between the two medians is the chrome and nothing else. Themed, this addon's draw and widget callbacks read ZERO over 15 sampled frames — the engine paints chrome from data parsed once, which is why a per-frame Lua Deco callback was rejected at design time — and the widget tree's own per-frame cost (utick + draw) stays what stock cost it, both medians printed in the line so the numbers travel with the verdict. Profiling answers only while armed, so when the switch is off that half becomes one [manual] line naming it; the switch is READ and never written. Two more [manual] lines close the feature on the deliverable itself: enable the `theme` addon and ':theme on' / ':theme dump' / ':theme off' for a whole client themed from JSON with no code of its own, and a drag/resize/close pass over a themed window. READ-ONLY: declares no permissions, mutates no persistent state, destroys its probe and drops its sheet before it finishes.
